item.title: The Cure’s Robert Smith Blasts FIFA’s World Cup Final Half-Time Show: ‘Please Just F— Off’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends in the music world. Today, we're talking about the FIFA World Cup final and a very unlikely critic: Robert Smith, the lead singer of The Cure. Smith is speaking out against the half-time show, curated by Chris Martin of Coldplay, which features some of the biggest names in music, including BTS, Justin Bieber, Shakira, and Madonna."
[Short music transition]
Host: "The half-time show is a first for the World Cup, and it's getting a lot of attention. But Smith is not a fan, calling it a 'groundbreaking spectacle' that's more about distraction than celebration. He took to The Cure's Instagram page to express his discontent, saying 'AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAGH...' and blasting FIFA's president, Gianni Infantino, for his involvement."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Smith clarified that he's not criticizing the artists themselves, but rather the concept of the half-time show and the fact that it's being used as a platform for FIFA's president and other dignitaries, including President Trump, who will be on hand to award the winner. Smith calls it 'bread and circuses' and says it's taking away from the true spirit of the game."
[Short music transition]
Host: "As a longtime fan of the sport, Smith's comments are getting a lot of attention. And it's not just him - many fans are booing the new 'hydration breaks' during the game, which some see as a disruption to the flow of the match. The World Cup final is set to take place on Sunday, with Argentina facing off against Spain at the New York/New Jersey Stadium."
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for today's podcast. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you next time with more news and updates from the world of music."
